title: Celigo connection
description: Fields that can be sent when creating or updating a connection.

x-celigo-ai-guidance: Name the connection after the ONE system it authenticates to — the application, plus the account, store, or environment when that distinguishes it (e.g. "Shopify - mystore", "NetSuite Non-Production").

Never name a connection after a flow or use case, and never include a second application in the name (not "Shopify to NetSuite Customer Sync"). Connections are account-level resources reused across many integrations; a use-case name hides which system the credentials belong to and misleads later reuse.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Server requires a non-empty name and rejects values longer than the declared maxLength. Bounds mirror live server enforcement.

type.description: Connection type, which determines the authentication and connectivity options available and which config object must be supplied.

x-enumDescriptions.netsuite: NetSuite ERP connection using token-based authentication (TBA).
x-enumDescriptions.salesforce: Salesforce CRM connection with OAuth 2.0 authentication.
x-enumDescriptions.ftp: FTP, SFTP, or FTPS file transfer connection.
x-enumDescriptions.wrapper: Wrapper connection that delegates to another connection type.
x-enumDescriptions.http: Generic HTTP/REST API connection with full configuration control.
x-enumDescriptions.rdbms: Relational database connection (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, etc.).
x-enumDescriptions.filesystem: Local or network filesystem connection (requires an Agent).
x-enumDescriptions.jdbc: JDBC database connection for systems not covered by RDBMS.
x-enumDescriptions.van: Value-Added Network connection for EDI document exchange.
x-enumDescriptions.rest: REST connection driven by a pre-built HTTP Connector template. Deprecated — use `http` instead.

externalId.description: External identifier for the connection, often used to correlate it with a record in a third-party system.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Free user-chosen correlation value — no vocabulary or pattern to encode.

assistant.description:
Lowercase application name for HTTP connections to systems with an integrator.io
adaptor (e.g. "shopify", "ebay"). Only applies to http connections.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Open application-slug vocabulary — new adaptors mint new slugs; do not freeze the observed set.

_agentId.description:
Reference to a Celigo on-premise Agent. Required for types that need local network or
filesystem access (filesystem, jdbc agent/activedirectory, Oracle rdbms, and on-premise
mongodb). The agent establishes a secure tunnel between the on-premise environment and
integrator.io.

_agentGroupId.description:
On-premise agent group that serves this connection instead of a single
`_agentId` — mutually exclusive with it. Requests go to the first
healthy member in the group's priority order, so one host failing does
not stop the flow. Available once agent groups are generally available.

_borrowConcurrencyFromConnectionId.description:
Reference to another connection to share concurrency limits with. When set, this
connection's traffic counts against the referenced connection's limit instead of its own,
and its own concurrency and auto-recovery settings have no effect. One level only: the
referenced connection may not itself borrow, and a connection that others borrow from
cannot start borrowing.

autoRecoverRateLimitErrors.description:
When true, rate-limit errors from the target system trigger automatic recovery — concurrency
drops to 1 and climbs back toward the adaptor block's `targetConcurrencyLevel`, which is the
throughput lever while this is on. Turning it on copies the current `concurrencyLevel` into
the target; turning it off unsets the target and leaves `concurrencyLevel` at its current value.

__integrationIds.description:
Integrations to register the new connection on immediately after creation, making it
available for use within them. Only honored on `POST /v1/connections` (ignored on PUT)
and never persisted on the connection document. Ids are validated before the connection
is saved; registration runs after the save, and per-integration failures are reported in
`__failedIntegrationRegistrations` on the 201 response without rolling back the new
connection.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Invalid input rejects the whole request without creating the connection: a non-array value
or duplicate ids fail with 422 invalid_request, an element that is not a valid ObjectId fails
with 422 invalid_ref naming __integrationIds[i], an integration that does not exist in the
account fails with 404, and more than 100 ids fails with 400 batch_size_exceeded.

Integrations installed through an Integration App cannot be registered this way — the
connection is still created (201) and the failure is reported in
__failedIntegrationRegistrations with code not_allowed.

endUserProvidedFields.description:
Dot-paths of this connection's fields (for example `http.encrypted.apiKey` or
`rdbms.user`) that each MCP end user must supply on their own `mcpChild` copy instead of
inheriting the parent's value. Set it on the parent connection an MCP server collects
end-user credentials for; omit it everywhere else. Omitting it (or sending `[]`) on
`PUT` keeps the stored paths; send `null` to clear them. By the platform contract,
changing the stored list — adding, removing, or clearing paths — invalidates the
`mcpChild` connections end users already hold against this parent, so each of them
sets up again through the MCP setup page before tools that use it run for them.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
List only the credential and tenant fields that differ per end user, never a path the
account owns: `type`, `_agentId`, `wrapper._stackId`, or any `<adaptor>._iClientId`
(e.g. `http._iClientId`) fails the save with 422
`mcp_end_user_provided_field_not_allowed`.

This is the only MCP end-user field writable through `/v1/connections`; the child
connections themselves are created by the end-user setup page, and `connectionRole:
mcpChild` in a `POST` or `PUT` body fails with 422 `mcp_child_generic_route_not_allowed`.

debugDate.description: Enables debug logging until this timestamp. Set to a future time to capture request/response logs.

settingsForm.description: Dynamic form definition for connection-specific custom settings.

settings.description:
Connection-specific settings captured by settingsForm. At runtime, steps using
this connection read the values under the fixed scope key `connection` — e.g.
`{{settings.connection.<fieldId>}}` in Handlebars or
`$.settings.connection.<fieldId>` in Mapper 2.0 envelope references.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Freeform user payload by design — interiors deliberately unconstrained; do not model keys.

pgp.description: Present for file-based connections (ftp, s3, filesystem, …) that encrypt or decrypt files with PGP.

publicKey.description:
ASCII-armored PGP public key used to encrypt outbound files before upload.
Set this when the connection sends encrypted files; omit it for decrypt-only connections.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Public key for JWT verification. Optional — used when the API requires
the public key to be registered for signature verification.

privateKey.description:
ASCII-armored PGP private key used to decrypt inbound files after download (encrypted at rest;
returned masked as `"******"`). Set this when the connection receives encrypted files.

passphrase.description: Passphrase that unlocks `privateKey` (encrypted at rest; returned masked as `"******"`). Set this whenever `privateKey` is provided.

x-enumDescriptions.zip: ZIP compression — the most widely compatible option.

compressionAlgorithm.description: Compression applied to the message payload before PGP encryption. Match the algorithm the recipient expects; leave unset to use the server default.

asciiArmored.description: When true, produces ASCII-armored (text) PGP output. Set to false only when the recipient requires binary PGP output.

ssl.description:
SSL/TLS certificate configuration for database connections that use client certificate
(mTLS) authentication or connect to servers with private CA-signed certificates. Provide
cert and key together for mTLS, ca for a private CA, and passphrase only when the private
key is encrypted; cert/key and ca can be combined.

ca.description:
Certificate Authority certificate in PEM format. Set when the database server uses a
certificate signed by a private CA not in the system's default trust store.

key.description:
Client private key in PEM format, paired with cert for mTLS authentication.
Cannot be provided without cert.

passphrase.description: Passphrase that decrypts the private key in the key field, when that key is password-protected.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Passphrase to decrypt an encrypted private key (encrypted at rest).
Only needed when the PEM private key in the key field is password-protected.

cert.description:
Client certificate in PEM format, paired with key for mTLS authentication.
Cannot be provided without key.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Used by RDBMS and other connection types that support client certificate authentication
or connections to servers with private CA-signed certificates.

## USAGE RULES
- Provide cert + key together for client certificate (mutual TLS) authentication.
- Provide ca alone when the server uses a certificate signed by a private CA.
- cert/key and ca can be combined for mTLS with a private CA.
- passphrase is only needed when the private key is encrypted.

x-enumDescriptions.basic: Legacy email and password authentication (not recommended for new connections).
x-enumDescriptions.token: Manual Token-Based Authentication (TBA) using tokenId and tokenSecret from a NetSuite integration record.
x-enumDescriptions.token-auto: Automatic token management via Celigo's iClient; requires only the NetSuite account ID.

authType.description:
Authentication method for the NetSuite connection. token-auto delegates the token
lifecycle to an iClient; token uses a manually-supplied tokenId/tokenSecret pair.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Default to "token-auto" for new connections, including placeholders (only the account id is needed).
Use "token" when the user supplies their own tokenId/tokenSecret. Do not create "basic" connections:
the API rejects them with 422 "netsuite_wsdl_tba_mandatory" because the available WSDL versions
require Token-Based Authentication.

account.description:
NetSuite account ID (automatically uppercased), required for token and token-auto authentication.
Found in NetSuite under Setup > Company > Company Information. Non-production accounts
carry an environment suffix (e.g. `123456_SB1`); production and beta use the bare id.

x-enumDescriptions.production: Connect to the live production NetSuite instance.
x-enumDescriptions.sandbox: Connect to a legacy NetSuite sandbox account.
x-enumDescriptions.sandbox2.0: Connect to a NetSuite SuiteCloud (SB2.0) sandbox account.
x-enumDescriptions.beta: Connect to the NetSuite beta/release-preview environment.

environment.description: NetSuite environment to connect to. Defaults to production when not specified.

tokenId.description:
NetSuite TBA token ID (encrypted at rest). Required when authType is "token".

Generated in NetSuite under Setup > Users/Roles > Access Tokens.
Must be paired with the corresponding tokenSecret.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Not needed when authType is "token-auto" — integrator.io manages the token wiring in that mode.

tokenSecret.description:
NetSuite TBA token secret (encrypted at rest). Required when authType is "token".

Generated alongside the tokenId in NetSuite. Treat as a sensitive credential.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Not needed when authType is "token-auto".

entityId.description: NetSuite entity/user ID associated with the token.

tokenName.description: Human-readable name of the NetSuite access token for identification purposes.

roleId.description:
NetSuite role ID that determines the permissions for this connection.

The role controls which records, fields, and operations are accessible.
Must match the role associated with the access token in NetSuite.

email.description:
NetSuite user email address. Required when authType is "basic".
Used as the login credential for basic (email/password) authentication.

password.description: NetSuite user password (encrypted at rest). Required when authType is "basic".

requestLevelCredentials.description:
When true, authentication credentials are sent with each individual API request
rather than maintaining a persistent session. The connection form sets this to true
for token (manual TBA) authentication.

useSsoLogin.description:
Legacy single-sign-on login flag for the deprecated basic (email/password) auth flow. Not exposed
by the current connection form and not settable via the API (writes are silently dropped); retained
for the existing connections that carry it. New connections use token-based authentication instead.

dataCenterURLs.description:
NetSuite data center URLs for the account, auto-discovered from the account ID.
These are populated by the server after a successful connection.

restDomain.description: Base URL for the account's RESTlet and REST API endpoints.

webservicesDomain.description: Base URL for the account's SuiteTalk (SOAP) web services endpoints.

systemDomain.description: Base URL for the account's NetSuite UI/system endpoints.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
NetSuite data center URL overrides. Normally auto-discovered from the account ID.
Only set this to override the default data center routing.

accountName.description: Human-readable NetSuite account name (display purposes only).

roleName.description: Human-readable name of the NetSuite role (display purposes only).

wsdlVersion.description:
SuiteTalk Web Services WSDL version. The API stores only `latest` or `next`; any other value sent
on create or update is normalized to one of these (the connection form's "2025.1" maps to `latest`
and "2023.1" maps to `next`; unrecognized version strings fall back to `latest`). Defaults to
`latest`, which requires Token-Based Authentication.

x-enumDescriptions.latest: Current default WSDL release. Shown in the connection form as "2025.1".
x-enumDescriptions.next: Alternate WSDL release. Shown in the connection form as "2023.1".

applicationId.description:
NetSuite application ID from the integration record.
Required for some authentication configurations to identify the calling application.

concurrencyLevelRESTlet.description:
Deprecated per-endpoint cap on concurrent NetSuite RESTlet requests, superseded by the unified
`concurrencyLevel`. Server-reported only — values sent on create or update are silently dropped
(live-verified); retained for existing connections.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Maximum concurrent requests to NetSuite RESTlet endpoints.
NetSuite enforces governance limits on concurrent RESTlet requests per account.
Keep this low to avoid SuiteScript governance errors.

concurrencyLevelWebServices.description:
Deprecated per-endpoint cap on concurrent NetSuite SuiteTalk Web Services (SOAP) requests, superseded
by the unified `concurrencyLevel`. Server-reported only — values sent on create or update are
silently dropped (live-verified); retained for existing connections.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Maximum concurrent requests to NetSuite SuiteTalk Web Services (SOAP API).
NetSuite enforces concurrency limits per account — exceeding them causes
"Only one request may be made against a session at a time" errors.

concurrencyLevel.description:
General concurrency level for this connection. Controls the overall
maximum concurrent requests across all operation types.
Values above the account's licensed maximum (25 standard, 50 with an Environments license) are silently clamped down.

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Target concurrency level for auto-scaling. The system adjusts concurrency
between 1 and this value based on rate limit and governance feedback.

_iClientId.description: ID of the iClient used for token-based authentication.

sandbox.description:
Whether this connection targets a Salesforce non-production (sandbox) org. When true,
authenticates against test.salesforce.com instead of login.salesforce.com. Must match
the actual Salesforce org type or authentication fails. This is the form's
production-vs-sandbox selector (distinct from the connection-level `sandbox` flag).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
- true — Uses test.salesforce.com for authentication.
- false — Uses login.salesforce.com for authentication (production).

x-enumDescriptions.jwtBearerToken: Server-to-server JWT Bearer Token flow; requires a Connected App with a digital certificate and the username field.
x-enumDescriptions.refreshToken: Authorization Code / Refresh Token flow; requires initial browser-based authorization, then the refresh token for ongoing access.

oauth2FlowType.description:
OAuth 2.0 authentication flow type. Use jwtBearerToken for automated server-to-server
integrations (requires a Connected App with a digital certificate and the username field).
Use refreshToken for integrations that operate in a specific user's context. Defaults to
refreshToken when omitted.

username.description:
Salesforce login username (email) of the user whose permissions the integration operates
under. Used by the jwtBearerToken flow to identify the subject of the assertion.
username.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form when oauth2FlowType is jwtBearerToken (the form hides this field for the refreshToken flow). The API enforces neither the requirement nor the flow gating — it stores username whenever sent.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Salesforce username for JWT Bearer Token authentication.
REQUIRED when oauth2FlowType is "jwtBearerToken".

_iClientId.description:
Reference to the iClient holding your own Salesforce Connected App's client ID and secret.
Set this to authenticate through a custom Connected App; omit it to use Celigo's
pre-configured Connected App.

baseURI.description:
Salesforce instance URL for this org (e.g. "https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com").
Auto-discovered and populated during OAuth authentication; set it explicitly only to
force a specific instance URL.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Normally auto-discovered during OAuth authentication. Only set this to
force a specific instance URL (e.g., "https://mycompany.my.salesforce.com").

bearerToken.description:
OAuth access token for Salesforce API calls (encrypted at rest; returned masked as
`"******"`). Auto-managed by the system during the OAuth flow; rarely set manually.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
OAuth access/bearer token (encrypted at rest).
Typically auto-managed by the system during OAuth flows. Rarely set manually.

refreshToken.description:
OAuth refresh token used to mint new access tokens (encrypted at rest; returned masked as
`"******"`). Obtained during the initial browser-based authorization of the refreshToken
flow; auto-managed by the system.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
OAuth refresh token (encrypted at rest). REQUIRED when oauth2FlowType is "refreshToken".
Obtained during the initial browser-based OAuth authorization flow.

When true, uses Celigo's pre-configured Connected App for OAuth.
When false, you must provide your own Connected App credentials via iClient.

scope.description:
OAuth scopes requested during authorization. Scope values are defined by Salesforce — `full`
grants complete API access and `refresh_token` enables long-lived refresh tokens. Defaults
to `full` and `refresh_token` when omitted. A saved empty array is the normal stored state:
the connection form does not expose this field, and every save from the connection editor
resets values written through the API.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Never set or repair this field to fix an authentication failure: an empty or absent list is the normal stored state, and UI saves reset API-written values.

For a custom Connected App (`salesforce._iClientId` set), requested scopes are configured on the iClient's `oauth2.scope` and constrained by the Connected App inside Salesforce — not on the connection.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of concurrent API requests to Salesforce. Salesforce enforces per-org API
request limits, so setting this high consumes the org's API call allocation faster. Values
above the licensed ceiling are silently clamped (live-verified: a request for 999 is stored
as 50).

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Upper bound for auto-scaling concurrency. When automatic rate-limit recovery is enabled, the
system adjusts concurrency between 1 and this value based on rate-limit feedback from
Salesforce. Values above the licensed ceiling are silently clamped to 50.
targetConcurrencyLevel.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form, but only shown (and only applicable) when autoRecoverRateLimitErrors is true and no concurrency is borrowed from another connection. The API does not enforce it and defaults it to 5.

x-enumDescriptions.ftp: Standard FTP with no transport encryption (default port 21).
x-enumDescriptions.sftp: SSH-based file transfer with encrypted transport (default port 22); supports SSH key auth via authKey.
x-enumDescriptions.ftps: FTP over TLS/SSL with encrypted transport; port 21 for explicit TLS or 990 for implicit (useImplicitFtps).

type.description:
File transfer protocol type. Prefer sftp for security. Use ftps when the
server requires TLS. Only use ftp for legacy systems without encryption support.

hostURI.description:
FTP server hostname or IP address.
Do NOT include the protocol prefix (e.g., use "ftp.example.com", not "sftp://ftp.example.com").

port.description:
Server port number. When omitted, defaults to the standard port for the
protocol: 21 for ftp, 22 for sftp, 21 for explicit ftps, and 990 for implicit ftps.

password.description:
Password for server authentication (encrypted at rest; returned masked as `"******"`).
For sftp, supply either password or authKey (SSH key).
password.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form: a password for ftp/ftps, or a password or SSH key (authKey) for sftp (see the if/then/else rule below). Encoded here to mirror the form so builders produce complete, connectable configurations.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: For ftp/ftps set password; for sftp set password or authKey. The connection cannot authenticate without credentials.

authKey.description:
SSH private key for SFTP key-based authentication (encrypted at rest; returned masked as `"******"`).
Only used when type is "sftp". Provide the full PEM-encoded private key.
Can be used alone or alongside a password for two-factor auth.

usePassiveMode.description:
When true, uses passive mode for FTP/FTPS data connections.
In passive mode, the client initiates both control and data connections,
which works better through firewalls and NAT. Enable for most scenarios.

enableHostVerification.description:
When true, verifies the server's SSH host key (sftp) or TLS certificate (ftps).
Disable only for development/testing with self-signed certificates.

userDirectoryIsRoot.description:
When true, treats the user's home directory as the root directory.
All paths are relative to the user's home directory rather than the server root.

useImplicitFtps.description:
When true, uses implicit FTPS (TLS connection established immediately on port 990).
When false, uses explicit FTPS (starts as FTP on port 21, upgrades to TLS via STARTTLS).
Only applies when type is "ftps".

requireSocketReUse.description:
When true, requires the data connection to reuse the same TLS session as the control connection.
Some FTPS servers require this for security. Only applies to FTPS connections.

x-enumDescriptions.UNIX: Standard Unix/Linux directory listing format (most common).
x-enumDescriptions.UNIX-TRIM: Unix format with trimmed whitespace for non-standard servers.
x-enumDescriptions.WINDOWS: Windows FTP server DOS-style directory listing format.
x-enumDescriptions.MVS: IBM mainframe MVS directory listing format.
x-enumDescriptions.UNKNOWN-TYPE: Attempt automatic detection of the listing format.
x-enumDescriptions.MACOS-PETER: macOS Peter's FTP server directory listing format.

entryParser.description:
File listing format parser. Controls how directory listings from the server are interpreted.
Most servers use UNIX format. Only change this if directory listings appear garbled.

pgpEncryptKey.description:
Deprecated: legacy FTP-scoped PGP public key. Superseded by the connection-level `pgp.publicKey`,
which the current form writes; retained for the few existing connections still on this path
(encrypted at rest).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
PGP public key for encrypting files before upload (encrypted at rest).
When set, files are PGP-encrypted before being sent to the server.

pgpDecryptKey.description:
Deprecated: legacy FTP-scoped PGP private key. Superseded by the connection-level `pgp.privateKey`;
retained for the few existing connections still on this path (encrypted at rest).
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
PGP private key for decrypting files after download (encrypted at rest).
When set, downloaded files are automatically PGP-decrypted.

pgpPassphrase.description: Deprecated: legacy FTP-scoped PGP passphrase. Superseded by the connection-level `pgp.passphrase` (encrypted at rest; returned masked as `"******"`).

x-enumDescriptions.3DES: Triple DES symmetric cipher (168-bit effective key strength).
x-enumDescriptions.AES-128: AES symmetric cipher with a 128-bit key.
x-enumDescriptions.AES-192: AES symmetric cipher with a 192-bit key.
x-enumDescriptions.AES-256: AES symmetric cipher with a 256-bit key (strongest option).

pgpKeyAlgorithm.description:
Deprecated: legacy FTP-scoped PGP encryption-algorithm selector, no longer exposed by the
connection form (the current `pgp` object has no algorithm field). Retained for existing
connections. AES-256 is the strongest option; CAST5 is the PGP default.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Symmetric encryption algorithm used for PGP operations.
AES-256 is recommended for strong encryption. CAST5 is the PGP default.
Must match the algorithm expected by the recipient when encrypting.

pgpSignAndVerify.description:
Deprecated: legacy FTP-scoped PGP sign/verify toggle, no longer exposed by the connection form.
When true, PGP-signs outbound files and verifies signatures on inbound files. Retained for
existing connections.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
When true, PGP-signs outbound files and verifies signatures on inbound files.
Provides authenticity and integrity verification on top of encryption.

tradingPartner.description:
When true, this connection is designated a B2B/EDI trading partner. Read-only on the connection
body — POST/PUT of this field are silently ignored; it is toggled via
`PUT /connections/{_id}/tradingPartner` (used by the EDI B2B Manager).

_tpConnectorId.description:
Reference to the trading partner connector this connection belongs to. Must reference an
existing, published trading partner connector; the API rejects an unknown or unpublished ID
with 422 `tpconnector_not_found`.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of concurrent file transfer operations.
FTP servers often have low connection limits — keep this value conservative.
Values above the account's licensed maximum (25 standard, 50 with an Environments license) are silently clamped down.
Unlike the rest of the `ftp` object, a `PUT` that omits this field keeps the stored value instead of clearing it.

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Target concurrency level for auto-scaling. The system adjusts concurrency
between 1 and this value based on server response feedback.
Kept on a `PUT` that omits it, like `concurrencyLevel`; unset by the save while
`autoRecoverRateLimitErrors` is false.

multiThreadCount.description:
Number of parallel transfer threads for this FTP connection. Must be a
whole number — decimals are rejected on save. Values above the
account's licensed concurrency maximum are silently clamped down. On
save the value is mirrored into `userConcurrencyLevel` (and into
`userTargetConcurrencyLevel` when auto-recovery of rate-limit errors
is active with `targetConcurrencyLevel` set); clearing it clears the
mirrors. Not preserved across a `PUT` — re-send it with the rest of
the `ftp` object or it is cleared.

userConcurrencyLevel.description:
Server-maintained mirror of `multiThreadCount`. Present when
`multiThreadCount` is set; do not send it — it is recomputed on save.

x-enumDescriptions.accesskey: Authenticate with a static IAM access key pair (accessKeyId + secretAccessKey).
x-enumDescriptions.awsIam: Authenticate with AWS IAM role credentials supplied by a referenced iClient (_iClientId).

authType.description:
Authentication method for the S3 bucket. Defaults to `accesskey` when omitted. Use `awsIam`
to delegate authentication to an iClient that holds an AWS IAM role instead of embedding a
static key pair.

accessKeyId.description:
AWS access key ID for IAM authentication. From an IAM user or role with S3 permissions
(s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject, s3:ListBucket, etc.). Used when authType is `accesskey`.
accessKeyId.x-celigo-ui-override: The connection form marks accessKeyId required (the form only exposes static-key auth). The API enforces it for authType `accesskey` (POST without it returns 422 missing_required_field) — encoded via the if/then/else rule below.

secretAccessKey.description: AWS secret access key, paired with accessKeyId. Used when authType is `accesskey`. Encrypted at rest; returned masked as `"******"`.
secretAccessKey.x-celigo-ui-override: The connection form marks secretAccessKey required (the form only exposes static-key auth). The API enforces it for authType `accesskey` (POST without it returns 422 missing_required_field) — encoded via the if/then/else rule below.

_iClientId.description:
Reference to an iClient that holds AWS IAM role credentials. Required when authType is
`awsIam`; ignored otherwise.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: The referenced iClient must itself be an awsIam-provider iClient; referencing any other iClient fails the POST with 422 "IClient provider must be awsIam for S3 IAM Role authentication."

pingBucket.description:
S3 bucket name used for connection health checks (ping). The system performs a HEAD request
on this bucket to verify credentials. Must be a bucket the credentials have access to.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of concurrent S3 operations. Applies when `autoRecoverRateLimitErrors` is
false; when auto-recover is on (the default) concurrency auto-scales up to
`targetConcurrencyLevel` and a `concurrencyLevel` sent on its own is reconciled back. Values
above the account's licensed maximum are clamped down.

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Upper bound for auto-scaled concurrency when `autoRecoverRateLimitErrors` is true (the
default). The system raises and lowers concurrency between 1 and this value based on
rate-limit feedback from S3.

x-enumDescriptions.xml: Serialize request bodies as application/xml; use for SOAP or XML APIs.
x-enumDescriptions.json: Serialize request bodies as application/json; use for most modern REST APIs.
x-enumDescriptions.urlencoded: Serialize request bodies as application/x-www-form-urlencoded; use for form-style POST bodies.
x-enumDescriptions.form-data: Serialize request bodies as multipart/form-data; use for file uploads.
x-enumDescriptions.plaintext: Send request bodies as text/plain with no serialization.

mediaType.description:
Default content type for outbound HTTP request bodies.
Controls the Content-Type header and how request bodies are serialized.
x-celigo-ai-guidance: Default mediaType to "json" unless the API documentation specifies otherwise.

x-enumDescriptions.plaintext: Treat successful responses as raw text with no parsing.

successMediaType.description:
Expected content type of successful API responses. Controls how response bodies are parsed.
If omitted, the system infers the format from the response Content-Type header.

x-enumDescriptions.plaintext: Treat error responses as raw text with no parsing.

Expected content type of error responses from the API. Controls how error response bodies are parsed for extracting error messages.

baseURI.description:
Base URL for all API requests made through this connection. Required.

All relative URIs in exports and imports are appended to this base URL.
Must be an absolute URL (e.g., "https://api.example.com/v2").
Handlebars expressions are supported for dynamic URLs — e.g.
"https://{{{connection.settings.subdomain}}}.example.com".

disableStrictSSL.description:
When true, disables strict SSL/TLS certificate validation for API requests.

Only set to true for development/testing with self-signed certificates.
NEVER disable in production — it removes protection against man-in-the-middle attacks.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of concurrent HTTP requests this connection can make simultaneously.

Higher values increase throughput but may trigger API rate limits.
Set this based on the target API's rate limit documentation.
Values above the account's licensed maximum (25 standard, 50 with an Environments license) are silently clamped down,
but a decimal is rejected with 422 `invalid_field_value` on every write (the same rule applies to every
adaptor's `concurrencyLevel` and `targetConcurrencyLevel`, and to `ftp.multiThreadCount`).

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Ceiling the platform climbs back to after rate-limit recovery, in steps of 25% of this value.
Writing it also sets `concurrencyLevel` to the same value and stops any recovery in progress.

Honored only while `autoRecoverRateLimitErrors` is true; ignored, and unset, when it is false.

retryHeader.description:
HTTP response header name that contains the retry delay (in seconds) when rate-limited.

uses a non-standard header name for retry-after values.

oauth.description:
OAuth 2.0 and OAuth 1.0a authentication configuration.

x-enumDescriptions.assistant: Pre-configured OAuth settings via an application assistant connector.

OAuth configuration mode. Controls whether settings are user-configured or
pre-populated by an application assistant connector.

x-enumDescriptions.clientcredentials: Client Credentials flow for server-to-server authentication without user involvement.
x-enumDescriptions.password: Resource Owner Password Credentials flow exchanging username and password for tokens.

OAuth 2.0 grant type that determines the authentication flow.

server-to-server, and password only when the API does not support other flows.

OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint URL.

to authorize the application.

OAuth 2.0 token endpoint URL.

When true, skips Celigo's built-in OAuth configuration validation.
Use when the API has non-standard OAuth requirements that conflict with validation rules.

OAuth scopes to request during authorization. Controls the level of API access.
Scope values are API-specific (e.g., "read", "write", "admin").

Delimiter between multiple scope values. Defaults to a space (" ") per the
OAuth 2.0 spec. Some APIs use commas or other delimiters.

OAuth client ID (application ID) registered with the API provider.
Required for all OAuth 2.0 grant types.

OAuth client secret (encrypted at rest).
Required for "authorizecode" and "clientcredentials" grant types.

password.description: Resource owner password (encrypted at rest). Required when grantType is "password".

x-enumDescriptions.body: Send client credentials as form parameters in the request body.

(HTTP Basic Auth), which is recommended by the OAuth spec. Use body when
the API does not support Basic Auth for client credentials.

JSON path to extract the access token from the token endpoint response.

Additional HTTP headers to include in token endpoint requests.

instead of the values in this configuration.

OAuth 1.0a configuration for legacy APIs that use the older OAuth protocol.
Always needs consumerKey and accessToken; HMAC signature methods also need
consumerSecret and tokenSecret, while RSA methods need consumerPrivateKey.

consumerKey.description:
OAuth 1.0a consumer key (API key).
Identifies the application making the request.

consumerSecret.description:
OAuth 1.0a consumer secret (encrypted at rest).
Required for HMAC and PLAINTEXT signature methods.

accessToken.description:
OAuth 1.0a access token (encrypted at rest).
Represents the user's authorization for the application to access their data.

tokenSecret.description:
OAuth 1.0a token secret (encrypted at rest).
Required for HMAC and PLAINTEXT signature methods.

x-enumDescriptions.hmac-sha1: HMAC signing with SHA-1 (most widely supported, legacy).
x-enumDescriptions.hmac-sha256: HMAC signing with SHA-256 for improved security.
x-enumDescriptions.hmac-sha512: HMAC signing with SHA-512 (strongest HMAC variant).
x-enumDescriptions.rsa-sha256: RSA signing with SHA-256 for improved security.
x-enumDescriptions.rsa-sha512: RSA signing with SHA-512 (strongest RSA variant).
x-enumDescriptions.plaintext: No cryptographic signing, only for testing over HTTPS.

signatureMethod.description:
OAuth 1.0a request signing method. HMAC methods require consumerSecret and
tokenSecret; RSA methods require consumerPrivateKey. PLAINTEXT offers no
cryptographic signing and should only be used for testing over HTTPS.

consumerPrivateKey.description:
RSA private key for OAuth 1.0a RSA signature methods (encrypted at rest).
Required when signatureMethod is RSA-SHA1, RSA-SHA256, or RSA-SHA512.

OAuth realm value included in the Authorization header.
Some APIs require this to identify the authentication domain.

- consumerKey (always required)
- accessToken (always required)
- For HMAC methods: consumerSecret and tokenSecret
- For RSA methods: consumerPrivateKey

PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) code verifier for enhanced OAuth 2.0 security.
Managed internally by the system during authorization code flows.

  Requires tokenURI, clientId, clientSecret.
- "password" — Resource Owner Password flow (username/password exchange).

session cookies from the response, and includes them in all subsequent API requests.

JWT Bearer authentication configuration. Used when auth.type is "jwtbearer" on HTTP
connections. The connection builds a JWT from payload and headers, signs it using
signatureMethod, and sends it as the bearer token. HMAC methods sign with secret;
RSA/ECDSA/PSS methods sign with privateKey.

x-enumDescriptions.hmac-sha384: HMAC with SHA-384 (symmetric); signs with secret.
x-enumDescriptions.hmac-sha512: HMAC with SHA-512 (symmetric); signs with secret.
x-enumDescriptions.rsa-sha256: RSA with SHA-256 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.rsa-sha384: RSA with SHA-384 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.rsa-sha512: RSA with SHA-512 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.es256: ECDSA with P-256 and SHA-256 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.es384: ECDSA with P-384 and SHA-384 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.es512: ECDSA with P-521 and SHA-512 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.ps256: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.ps384: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-384 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.
x-enumDescriptions.ps512: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-512 (asymmetric); signs with privateKey.

signatureMethod.description:
JWT signing method. Required when auth.type is "jwtbearer". HMAC methods require
the secret field; RSA/ECDSA/PSS methods require the privateKey field.

payload.description:
JWT claims payload (the token body). Required and must be non-empty when auth.type
is "jwtbearer". Keys are JWT claim names (e.g. iss, sub, aud, exp).

headers.description: JWT header parameters merged into the generated token header (e.g. kid).

Shared secret for HMAC signature methods (hmac-sha256/hmac-sha512), encrypted at rest.
Required when signatureMethod is an HMAC method.

privateKey.description:
PEM-encoded private key for RSA/ECDSA/PSS signature methods, encrypted at rest.
Required for any rsa-*, es*, or ps* signature method.

Private key in PEM format for RSA or ECDSA signing (encrypted at rest).
REQUIRED when using an RSA (RS*) or ECDSA (ES*) algorithm.
Not used with HMAC algorithms.

token.description:
Pre-generated static JWT to use instead of building one from payload (encrypted at rest).
Use only when the API issues a long-lived JWT that does not need regeneration.

Pre-generated JWT token value (encrypted at rest).
When set, this static token is used instead of generating one dynamically.
Use only when the API provides a long-lived JWT that does not need to be regenerated.

a signed JWT and uses it as a bearer token for API authentication.

- HMAC (HS256/HS384/HS512): Symmetric signing using a shared secret.
  Requires the secret field.
- RSA (RS256/RS384/RS512): Asymmetric signing using an RSA private key.
  Requires the privateKey field.
- ECDSA (ES256/ES384/ES512): Asymmetric signing using an elliptic curve private key.
  Requires the privateKey field.

- algorithm (signing algorithm)
- secret (for HMAC algorithms) OR privateKey (for RSA/ECDSA algorithms)
- At least one claim (issuer, subject, audience, or customClaims)

secretAccessKey.description: Secret access key paired with `accessKeyId`. Encrypted at rest and returned masked as `"******"`.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of DynamoDB requests this connection runs at once.

Values are silently clamped into the licensed range — below 1 is raised to 1, and above the
account maximum (25 standard, 50 with an Environments license) is lowered to that maximum.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Maximum number of concurrent DynamoDB operations.
DynamoDB throughput is governed by table-level read/write capacity units.

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Concurrency ceiling for auto-scaling. The system adjusts the active concurrency between 1
and this value based on rate-limit feedback. Only applied when `autoRecoverRateLimitErrors`
is enabled on the connection. Clamped the same way as `concurrencyLevel`.
targetConcurrencyLevel.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form (its targetConcurrencyLevel field is required and defaults to 5). The API does not enforce this — a POST that omits it succeeds and the server defaults it to 5. Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce complete configurations.

x-enumDescriptions.agent: Generic JDBC driver deployed on a Celigo Agent (requires driverPath).
x-enumDescriptions.netsuitejdbc: NetSuite SuiteAnalytics JDBC driver for reporting and analytics queries.
x-enumDescriptions.oracle:thin: Oracle Database via the Oracle Thin JDBC driver.
x-enumDescriptions.sqlserver: Microsoft SQL Server via the JTDS or Microsoft JDBC driver.
x-enumDescriptions.activedirectory: SQL Server with Active Directory authentication.
x-enumDescriptions.workday: Workday via JDBC for report and data access.

type.description:
JDBC driver/connection type. Selects which JDBC driver is used and determines
the required fields. Most JDBC connections require a Celigo on-premise Agent.

version.description: JDBC driver version. Used for driver compatibility when multiple versions are available.

host.description:
Database server hostname or IP address.
For NetSuite JDBC, use the SuiteAnalytics Connect hostname
(e.g., "account-id.connect.api.netsuite.com").

port.description: Database server port number. Default varies by driver type.
port.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form for activedirectory (default 389) and db2. The API enforces it for db2 (POST 422 "Expected field: port to be present") but not for activedirectory, where the server auto-defaults it to 389. Encoded to mirror the form so builders produce connectable configurations.

database.description: Database or catalog name. For Oracle, use the serviceName field instead.

password.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form for activedirectory connections; the API creates an activedirectory connection without it (form-derived, not API-enforced). For workday the password is enforced by the API itself, so it is encoded as an unconditional required on the workday branch rather than as a form override.

serviceName.description:
Oracle service name. Used instead of the database field for Oracle JDBC connections.
This is the TNS service name or pluggable database (PDB) service name.

x-enumDescriptions.wallet: Oracle Wallet authentication using an encrypted wallet file.

authType.description:
Authentication method for the JDBC connection. Defaults to customjdbc (username/password).
Use wallet for Oracle Wallet authentication with the wallet field.

wallet.description:
Oracle Wallet file contents (encrypted at rest).
Required when authType is "wallet". Contains the auto-login wallet (cwallet.sso)
with encrypted credentials for passwordless Oracle authentication.

driverPath.description:
File path to the JDBC driver JAR on the Celigo Agent.
Required when type is "agent" (generic JDBC).
The driver must be deployed on the agent before creating the connection.

properties.description:
Additional JDBC connection properties as name/value pairs.
These are passed directly to the JDBC driver as connection properties.
Use for driver-specific settings like SSL mode, connection timeout,
application name, etc.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of concurrent database connections.
JDBC connections often run through a single Agent, so keep this value
conservative to avoid overwhelming the Agent or database.
Values above the account's licensed maximum (25 standard, 50 with an Environments license) are silently clamped down.

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Target concurrency level for auto-scaling. The system adjusts the number of
concurrent connections between 1 and this value based on performance feedback.

as2Id.description:
AS2 identifier for this VAN station — the "From" identifier on outbound documents and the "To"
identifier on inbound. Must be unique across all integrator.io VAN connections; a duplicate fails
the create. Set once when the connection is created and cannot be changed afterward (writes on update
are ignored). Omit it to have the network assign one automatically.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
AS2 identifier for this VAN station. Used as the "From" identifier when sending
documents and the "To" identifier when receiving. Must be unique across all
integrator.io users. Cannot be changed after creation.

mailboxId.description:
Numeric mailbox identifier assigned by the VAN provider when the connection is provisioned.
Server-assigned and not writable — values sent on create or update are ignored.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
VAN mailbox identifier. Identifies the specific mailbox on the VAN provider
that this connection sends to and receives from.

contentBasedFlowRouter.description:
Routes inbound documents to different flows based on message content, for a connection shared across
multiple flows. The named function in the referenced script inspects each incoming document and returns
the flow to run. Omit to disable content-based routing.

function.description: Name of the exported function in the referenced script that returns the target flow for each inbound document.

_scriptId.description: ID of the script resource that contains the routing function. Must reference an existing script; an unknown ID fails the request with 422 `invalid_ref`.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Content-based routing configuration for inbound VAN documents.
Routes incoming documents to different flows based on document content
using a custom JavaScript function.

x-enumDescriptions.http: Communicate with the MCP server over HTTP.

protocol.description:
Transport protocol for communicating with the MCP server.
Currently only "http" is supported; the server sets this automatically and ignores other values.

serverURL.description:
MCP server endpoint URL. Must be a valid absolute URL
(e.g. "https://mcp-server.example.com/mcp").
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
MCP server endpoint URL. REQUIRED.
Must be a valid absolute URL (e.g., "https://mcp-server.example.com/mcp").
The system validates this as a proper URL.

timeout.description:
Request timeout in milliseconds for MCP tool invocations.
If the MCP server does not respond within this time, the request fails.
Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes) when omitted.

allowedTools.description:
Optional allowlist of MCP tool names that this connection may invoke.
When set, only tools in this list can be called. When omitted or empty,
all tools exposed by the MCP server are available.

http.description: HTTP transport configuration for the MCP connection, including authentication and headers.

_iClientId.description:
Reference to an OAuth iClient for OAuth-based MCP authentication.
Required when http.auth.type is "oauth".
_iClientId.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form for oauth auth; the OAuth authorization is completed after the connection is created.

auth.description:
Authentication configuration for the MCP connection. The auth.type field selects the
strategy. MCP supports only token, oauth, and custom — other HTTP auth types
(basic, wsse, cookie, jwt, etc.) are rejected with a 422.

x-enumDescriptions.token: API key or bearer token; set auth.token.token (sent via header, URL parameter, or request body).
x-enumDescriptions.oauth: OAuth 2.0; reference an OAuth iClient via http._iClientId and complete the authorization after the connection is created.
x-enumDescriptions.custom: No built-in auth; place credentials in http.headers or the http.encrypted / http.unencrypted custom fields.

type.description: Authentication method for the MCP server. Determines which auth sub-fields apply.

token.description:
Token-based authentication configuration. Required when auth.type is "token".

Supports static API keys/bearer tokens and automatic token refresh flows.
The token can be sent in a header (Authorization), query parameter, or request body.

The API key or bearer token value (encrypted at rest); returned masked as `"******"`.
Required unless automatic token refresh is configured.

x-enumDescriptions.url: Include the token as a URL query parameter.
x-enumDescriptions.header: Include the token in an HTTP header (most common).
x-enumDescriptions.body: Include the token in the request body.

location.description:
Where to include the token in outbound requests.
Most APIs expect header. Use headerName and scheme to control the header format,
or paramName when sending as a URL query parameter.
location.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form for token auth; the API accepts a static token without it.

headerName.description:
HTTP header name for the token when location is "header".
Defaults to "Authorization" if omitted.
headerName.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form when location is "header"; also where wsse auth stores its header name (default "X-WSSE"). The API does not enforce it.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Free-form header name chosen per target API — observed cardinality is poisoned by harness redaction; no vocabulary to encode.

scheme.description:
Token scheme/prefix when sent in a header. Prepended before the token value.
Common values: "Bearer", "Token", "Basic".
Example: scheme "Bearer" produces header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

x-celigo-canon.reason: Free-form scheme string — production includes a literal space value; do not freeze to the common Bearer/Token/Basic set.

paramName.description:
Query parameter name for the token when location is "url".
Example: paramName "api_key" produces URL "?api_key=<token>".

x-enumDescriptions.GET: Use a GET request to refresh the token.
x-enumDescriptions.POST: Use a POST request to refresh the token.
x-enumDescriptions.PUT: Use a PUT request to refresh the token.

refreshMethod.description:
HTTP method for automatic token refresh requests.
Required when no static token is provided (refresh-based auth flow).

refreshRelativeURI.description:
Relative URI (appended to baseURI) for the token refresh endpoint.
The system calls this endpoint to obtain a new token when the current one expires.

refreshBody.description: Request body to send with the token refresh request.

x-enumDescriptions.json: Send the refresh request body as application/json.
x-enumDescriptions.urlencoded: Send the refresh request body as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.
x-enumDescriptions.xml: Send the refresh request body as application/xml.
x-enumDescriptions.plaintext: Send the refresh request body as text/plain.

refreshMediaType.description: Content type for the token refresh request body.

x-enumDescriptions.json: Parse the token refresh response as JSON.
x-enumDescriptions.xml: Parse the token refresh response as XML.

refreshResponseMediaType.description: Expected content type of the token refresh response.

refreshTokenPath.description:
JSON path to extract the new token from the refresh response.
Example: "access_token" or "data.token".

refreshToken.description: Refresh token used to obtain a new access token (encrypted at rest).

x-enumDescriptions.header: Include the refresh token in an HTTP header.
x-enumDescriptions.body: Include the refresh token in the request body.

refreshTokenLocation.description: Where to include the refresh token in refresh requests.

name.description: Header name to send with the token-refresh request.

value.description: Header value to send with the token-refresh request.

refreshHeaders.description: Additional headers to include in token refresh requests.

tokenPaths.description:
JSON paths to extract multiple token values from the refresh response.
Use when the refresh response contains tokens at different paths that need
to be stored for subsequent requests.

revoke.description:
Token-revocation request configuration. When set, the system calls this
endpoint to revoke the current token (e.g. when the connection is deleted or
re-authenticated). Used mainly by pre-built HTTP Connector templates.

uri.description: Absolute URL of the token-revocation endpoint.

body.description: Request body to send with the token-revocation request.

headers.description: Additional headers to include in the token-revocation request.

name.description: Header name to send with the revocation request.

value.description: Header value to send with the revocation request.

headers.description: Default HTTP headers included in every request to the MCP server.

value.description: Header value. Supports handlebars expressions for dynamic values.

unencrypted.description: Unencrypted custom fields for non-sensitive MCP configuration.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Freeform user payload by design — do not model interiors.

encrypted.description:
Encrypted custom fields for sensitive MCP configuration. Sent as an object;
returned as the masked string `"******"` on responses.

x-celigo-ai-guidance:
The auth.type MUST be one of: "token", "oauth", or "custom".
Other auth types (basic, cookie, jwt, etc.) are not supported for MCP connections.

pingFunction.description:
Name of the JavaScript function on the Stack that tests connection health, invoked when
"Test Connection" is clicked. It should verify the credentials are valid and the target
system is reachable.
pingFunction.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form for standalone wrappers. The form hides it for connector-managed wrappers (when _connectorId is set), where the connector supplies it.
x-celigo-ai-guidance:
Name of the JavaScript function on the Stack that tests connection health.
This function is called when the user clicks "Test Connection" in the UI.
It should verify that the connection credentials are valid and the target
system is reachable.

unencrypted.description:
Unencrypted custom fields for non-sensitive configuration values.
These values are accessible to the wrapper code on the Stack at runtime.
Field definitions are specified in unencryptedFields.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Freeform user payload by design — wrapper code defines the keys; do not model interiors.

unencryptedFields.description: Metadata defining the unencrypted custom fields on this connection.

id.description: Field identifier — matches the key in the unencrypted object.

label.description: Human-readable label shown in the UI.

required.description: When true, the custom field defined by this entry is mandatory — a value for it must be supplied before the connection can be saved.

position.description: Display order in the UI form.

helpText.description: Tooltip text shown next to the field in the UI.

type.description:
Optional, legacy field-type hint. The wrapper form ignores it — it always renders these
custom fields as text inputs — so it is rarely set.

encrypted.description:
Encrypted custom fields for sensitive configuration values (API keys, passwords, etc.).
Sent as an object of field-name/value pairs; values are encrypted at rest and decrypted
only on the Stack at runtime. Returned as the masked string `"******"` on responses.
Field definitions are specified in encryptedFields.

encryptedFields.description: Metadata defining the encrypted custom fields on this connection.

id.description: Field identifier — matches the key in the encrypted object.

label.description: Human-readable label shown in the UI.

required.description: When true, the custom field defined by this entry is mandatory — a value for it must be supplied before the connection can be saved.

position.description: Display order in the UI form.

helpText.description: Tooltip text shown next to the field in the UI.
examples: Your API secret key from the vendor's developer console.

type.description:
Optional, legacy field-type hint. The wrapper form ignores it — it always renders these
custom fields as text inputs (masked) — so it is rarely set.

_stackId.description: Reference to the Celigo Stack whose server-side JavaScript implements this connection.
_stackId.x-celigo-ui-override: Required by the connection form for standalone wrappers (a Stack must be selected), so it is enforced as required on create. The API itself accepts a wrapper without it (POST 201), and connector-managed wrappers (with _connectorId) omit it — so it is not required on responses.

x-celigo-canon.reason: Create-required is a documented form mirror — the API accepts a wrapper without a stack, and most production wrappers are connector-managed without one by design.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of concurrent operations through this wrapper connection.
Values above the account's licensed maximum (25 standard, 50 with an Environments license) are silently clamped down.

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Target concurrency level for auto-scaling. The system adjusts concurrency
between 1 and this value based on performance feedback.

rest.description: Present when `type` is `rest`. Deprecated — superseded by `http` with a pre-built HTTP Connector template.

x-enumDescriptions.json: Serialize request and response bodies as application/json.
x-enumDescriptions.xml: Serialize request and response bodies as application/xml.
x-enumDescriptions.csv: Serialize request and response bodies as text/csv.

mediaType.description:
Default content type for API requests and responses.
Most REST connector templates default to json.

baseURI.description:
Base URL for all API requests. REQUIRED.
All relative URIs in exports and imports are appended to this base URL.
May be pre-populated by the HTTP Connector template, and may contain
Handlebars expressions (e.g. a `{{{connection.settings.subdomain}}}` segment).

x-enumDescriptions.basic: HTTP Basic Authentication using a username and password.
x-enumDescriptions.token: Bearer token or API key with optional automatic refresh.
x-enumDescriptions.oauth: OAuth 2.0 authentication with authorization code, client credentials, or password grant.
x-enumDescriptions.custom: No built-in auth; credentials are placed in headers or encrypted fields.
x-enumDescriptions.cookie: Cookie-based session authentication via a login endpoint.
x-enumDescriptions.hmac: HMAC signature authentication for request signing.
x-enumDescriptions.wsse: WS-Security UsernameToken authentication for SOAP APIs.
x-enumDescriptions.oauth1: OAuth 1.0a authentication with HMAC or RSA signatures.

authType.description:
Authentication method for this connection. Available methods depend on
the connector template. Each type requires specific credential sub-fields.

authURI.description:
OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint URI.
Used for OAuth authorization code flow where users authorize via browser.

oauthTokenURI.description:
OAuth 2.0 token endpoint URI.
Used to exchange authorization codes for access tokens and to refresh tokens.

disableStrictSSL.description:
When true, disables strict SSL/TLS certificate validation.
Only use for development/testing with self-signed certificates.

skipOauthValidations.description:
When true, skips Celigo's built-in OAuth configuration validation.
Use when the connector has non-standard OAuth requirements.

isHTTPProxy.description: When true, this REST connection acts as an HTTP proxy for another connection.

authHeader.description:
Custom HTTP header name for the authorization token.
Defaults to "Authorization". Change only if the API uses a non-standard header.

retryHeader.description:
HTTP response header name containing retry-after delay for rate-limited requests.
Defaults to "Retry-After" (HTTP standard).

x-enumDescriptions.MAC: Use the MAC (Message Authentication Code) authorization scheme.
x-enumDescriptions.OAuth: Use the OAuth authorization scheme prefix.
x-enumDescriptions.Bearer: Use the Bearer token authorization scheme (most common).
x-enumDescriptions.Hmac: Use the HMAC authorization scheme for signed requests.
Deprecated: a single space sends the token with no scheme prefix (stored by legacy connector templates).

authScheme.description:
Authorization header scheme/prefix prepended before the token value.
Produces headers like "Authorization: Bearer <token>".
Defaults to "Bearer" which is the most common scheme.

x-celigo-canon.reason: The scheme vocabulary is closed on purpose. The server stores arbitrary strings here, and legacy connector templates hold a bare space (kept in source, hidden from published docs) — neither is grounds to open the enum.

scope.description: OAuth scopes to request during authorization. Controls the level of API access granted.

scopeDelimiter.description:
Delimiter character between multiple OAuth scopes.
Defaults to a space (" ") per the OAuth 2.0 spec. Some APIs use commas.

concurrencyLevel.description:
Maximum number of concurrent API requests.
Set based on the target API's rate limit documentation.

targetConcurrencyLevel.description:
Target concurrency level for auto-scaling. The system adjusts concurrency
between 1 and this value based on rate limit feedback.

bearerToken.description:
Bearer token or API key for authentication (encrypted at rest).
Used when authType is "token".

refreshToken.description:
OAuth refresh token (encrypted at rest).
Used to obtain new access tokens when they expire.

x-enumDescriptions.header: Send the access token in the Authorization header.
x-enumDescriptions.url: Send the access token as a URL query parameter.

tokenLocation.description:
Where to include the access token in outbound requests.
Defaults to header. Use tokenParam to set the query parameter name when sending via url.

tokenParam.description: URL query parameter name for the access token when tokenLocation is "url".

basicAuth.description: Basic authentication credentials. REQUIRED when authType is "basic" or "wsse".

password.description: Password for Basic authentication (encrypted at rest).

cookieAuth.description:
Cookie-based session authentication configuration.
REQUIRED when authType is "cookie".

uri.description: Login endpoint URI. REQUIRED. The system sends a request here to obtain session cookies.

body.description: Request body for the login request (e.g., JSON with credentials).

method.description: HTTP method for the login request (typically POST).

successStatusCode.description: HTTP status code that confirms successful authentication.

x-enumDescriptions.POST: Use a POST request to refresh the token.
x-enumDescriptions.PUT: Use a PUT request to refresh the token.
x-enumDescriptions.GET: Use a GET request to refresh the token.

refreshTokenMethod.description: HTTP method for token refresh requests.

refreshTokenBody.description: Request body template for token refresh requests.

refreshTokenURI.description: URI for the token refresh endpoint.

refreshTokenPath.description:
JSON path to extract the new access token from the refresh response.
Example: "access_token" or "data.token".

x-enumDescriptions.json: Send the refresh request body as application/json.
x-enumDescriptions.urlencoded: Send the refresh request body as application/x-www-form-urlencoded.

refreshTokenMediaType.description: Content type for token refresh request bodies.

refreshTokenHeaders.description: Additional headers to include in token refresh requests.

headers.description:
Default HTTP headers included in every API request.
Use for API keys in custom headers, content negotiation, or required headers.

pingRelativeURI.description:
Relative URI (appended to baseURI) for connection health check requests.
Should be a lightweight endpoint (e.g., "/me", "/health").

pingSuccessPath.description:
JSON path to extract a success indicator from the ping response.
If the value matches one of pingSuccessValues, the ping succeeds.

pingSuccessValues.description: Values that indicate a successful ping at pingSuccessPath.

pingFailurePath.description: JSON path to extract a failure indicator from the ping response.

pingFailureValues.description: Values that indicate a failed ping at pingFailurePath.

x-enumDescriptions.GET: Send a GET request to the ping endpoint.
x-enumDescriptions.POST: Send a POST request to the ping endpoint.

pingBody.description: Request body for ping requests (when pingMethod is POST).
